message:
No, I'm the only one for my four classrooms. The rooms were all in a row; I got in at about 0705 and got the desks set up and made sure the wireless routers were working, and tested my laptop's wireless connectivity in each room. At 0720 or so, Cadets started to filter in, and at 0735 I had my section marchers distribute the exams and I quickly went from room to room as the exam started and answered questions and got them started. I used one of the middle rooms as my home base for the 3.5 hours, although some of my colleagues took their desks out into the halls to be more approachable. All the classroom doors stayed open and the cadets worked fairly steadily, and took stretch and bathroom and coffee breaks as they needed. Once they finished, they submitted the file to Blackboard, where it was made available to the three blind graders, and sent a back-up e-mail copy to me. There were complications -- garbled files, dropped connections, and the ongoing problematics of using 802.11i wireless with its problems handling scalability, rather than the 802.11g or 802.11b that everyone else uses -- but for the most part, it went fairly smoothly. I was pleasantly surprised.

As far as the proctoring issue goes -- well, they didn't see the prompt until they started, and it's hard to cheat on an essay exam when you submit online -- and besides, there's that honor code.
